I will plant a simple wheat-maize rotation on all the land I manage this year. If I were making this decision for myself in Quzhou County, I would not split into many crops. I know this system, it fits the local land and water conditions, and it spreads my work across the year in a way I can handle. I would keep winter wheat as the first crop because it is stable and familiar, then follow with summer maize because that is the safest way for me to keep the land fully used and protect total grain output. I would use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, apply fertilizer at moderate rates instead of pushing too hard, irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat is more sensitive at key stages here, and keep pest control simple with a small number of timely sprays. For tillage, I would use rotary tillage before wheat because it helps me make a clean seedbed, and I would use no-tillage for maize after wheat harvest to save time and preserve moisture.
